question: Should OpenClaw allow sandboxed requester sessions to start ACP host or worker sessions, and which trust boundary should own that capability?
rationale: The code can implement several shapes, but choosing between a host bridge, isolated ACP workers, nested sandboxing, or keeping the block is a security/product decision that automation should not make.

options.title: Prefer Isolated ACP Workers
options.body: Extend the execution-backend/profile design so ACP runs in a sandboxed worker or sidecar with explicit auth, workspace, secret, lifecycle, and cleanup rules before enabling sandboxed requesters.

options.title: Approve Audited Host Bridge
options.body: Add an opt-in host-side ACP proxy with narrow spawn/steer/cancel APIs, allowlisting, rate limits, and durable audit logs for operators who accept controlled privilege escalation.

options.title: Keep Current Block
options.body: Continue documenting that sandboxed sessions must use runtime="subagent" or run ACP-capable harnesses inside the container until a stronger design is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Prefer Isolated ACP Workers
recommendation.body: Extend the execution-backend/profile design so ACP runs in a sandboxed worker or sidecar with explicit auth, workspace, secret, lifecycle, and cleanup rules before enabling sandboxed requesters.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice is closest to the ACP runtime and sandbox-inheritance security boundary that osolmaz merged and co-authored in the current implementation history.
